valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E at the 12-month target date. An investor in mid-Nov 2027 prices fiscal 2028 (Oct 2028 year-end) non-GAAP diluted EPS, so each case uses FY2028 EPS x a P/E, per share in USD (US-listed common, no ADR conversion). Base year FY2026: revenue $34.45B, non-GAAP EPS $12.89 (GAAP $12.62); Q4 FY26 revenue $10.41B, non-GAAP EPS $4.16; Q1 FY27 guide revenue $11.1B +/- $0.5B (14-week quarter), EPS $4.35 +/- $0.20. Roughly 0.80B diluted shares (market cap about $302B at $380.95 per MarketBeat), held flat with buybacks offsetting dilution. Share count and FY2028 EPS are my estimates; I could not open the 10-K or the full release (403), so figures come from press summaries.

bear.driver: Wafer fab equipment growth fades after 2027 (management sees more than 30% growth in 2027) and an AI-capex digestion plus China export limits cut FY2028 EPS about 24% below the base.
bear.assumption: EPS $16.00 at 14x (trough-style multiple, in line with the Nov 2026 compression)

base.driver: FY2027 EPS near $19 (quarterly path $4.35 rising to about $5), then roughly 15% growth in FY2028 as AI logic, DRAM and advanced packaging spending continues.

bull.driver: WFE keeps growing strongly into 2028 with packaging and mature-node recovery, lifting EPS about 23% above the base.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $22 the $370.50 close implies 16.8x; the 4-name analyst average target of $521 implies 23.7x on base EPS, or EPS $27.4 at 19x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $22 (5.9 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Semiconductor Systems revenue growth and the Q1 FY27 non-GAAP EPS against the $4.35 guide midpoint, tracking the more than 30% 2027 WFE growth call.
valuation.next_disclosure: Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings, expected mid-February 2027 (date not confirmed).

analyst_notes: Four named analysts (UBS, JPMorgan, Needham, B. Riley) all kept Buy-equivalent ratings but cut targets by 8% to 32% after the Nov 12 report, mostly citing sector multiple compression; their $470-$640 targets average about $521, 41% above the close, versus 12.8% for the base case, a 28 pp gap that equals about 4.7 turns of P/E or 25% more EPS than modeled. Wells Fargo, Stifel, Bernstein, TD Cowen, Jefferies, Bank of America and RBC also moved targets ($500-$600) but I could not source analyst names, so they are excluded. Horizons are unverified, so no call enters the weighted target; B. Riley's date (Nov 9) comes from a secondary article and may be unreliable.
